body_text:
A direct proof of $P\Rightarrow Q$ assumes $P$ and derives $Q$.
A proof by contraposition derives $\neg P$ from $\neg Q$, using
the classical equivalence
$(P\Rightarrow Q)\iff(\neg Q\Rightarrow\neg P)$. A proof by
contradiction assumes the negation of the desired conclusion
and derives an impossibility. These are transformations of the
logical target, not licenses to omit intermediate
justification.
